title: Cadence Reserve Quota & Soft-Freeze Protocol for Cycle Staffing
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Problem: Historical cycle planning at Redwood shows recurring mid-cycle scope slippage caused by uncoordinated pull-ins from adjacent teams, ad-hoc production incidents, and uneven distribution of on-call surge load. Current reserve strategies are either too conservative (wasting capacity) or too brittle (insufficient buffer for emergent enterprise customers).

Proposal: Introduce a "Cadence Reserve Quota & Soft-Freeze Protocol" (CRQ-SF) to be piloted in the 2026-W10 cycle. CRQ-SF formalizes a lightweight, rolling reserve that: (1) assigns a small, rotating pool of 10% FTE-equivalent capacity per initiative as a reserve quota rather than fixed contingency; (2) applies a soft-freeze window (6 business days) where only critical bugfix and enterprise-impact work can be pulled; (3) names a rotating "reserve steward" who mediates cross-team requests and approves temporary reallocation; (4) exposes the reserve state in the Cycle Dashboard and alerts on reserve burn rate.

Goals: reduce mid-cycle scope cuts by 30%, reduce emergency cross-team pulls by 40%, and maintain >90% utilization on planned work while retaining a predictable democratic path for critical interrupts.
acceptance_criteria: CRQ-SF policy doc published in Confluence with steward roster and approval workflow
Cycle Dashboard updated to show reserve quota, burn rate, and steward actions
Pilot executed in 2026-W10 with two initiatives (Optimize Batching, Console Rollouts) and quantitative burn-rate tracked
Post-pilot retrospective with metrics: mid-cycle scope slippage, number of emergency pulls, planned work utilization, and stakeholder sentiment
Operational runbook for steward and emergency reallocation created and reviewed by Eng and Design leads
rollout_plan: Week 0 (planning): finalize steward roster and policy; add reserve quota field to initiative templates. Week 1 (pilot start): enable soft-freeze windows on two initiatives, deploy dashboard widgets, circulate quickstart for stewards. Weeks 2-3 (observe): steward mediates all reserve requests; weekly OKR sync to measure burn; collect PM/Eng/Design feedback. End of cycle: 90-minute retrospective + metrics review and decision on scale to full org. Rollout to full org contingent on meeting acceptance criteria or approved deviations.
open_questions: What exact accounting formula converts headcount to FTE-equivalent reserve for fractional contributors?
Should reserve steward have final approval or only advisory authority when conflicts arise between business priorities?
How will Dedicated/Private enterprise urgent demands (SLA-driven) bypass soft-freeze if needed?
What telemetry threshold (burn-rate or incident count) auto-prompts escalation to the on-call rota?
decisions: Pilot scope limited to two product initiatives to reduce noise and allow clearer measurement
Reserve size set at 10% of initiative capacity for pilot (tunable after retrospective)
Soft-freeze window chosen as 6 business days to balance shipping cadence and protection for scope
Steward will initially be a PM with tie-break authority, reviewed by Eng and Design leads after pilot
